note: GLOBALCIT's Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (EUI, 2025), coding the law in force on 1 January 2024 (A06a ISR 5; A06b ISR 5; L05 No provision): ordinary naturalisation after 3 years' residence; the applicant must give up other citizenships; a citizen keeps it on taking another. Reforms after that date are checked in the file's later sources, where a later source is given. Citizenship at birth is read from the same dataset's 2024 coding of modes A01a (descent, born in country: Generally applicable provision), A01b (descent, born abroad: Generational transmission restriction: conditional on birthplace/place of residence /mode under which parent acquired citizenship), A02a (birth in country: Group restriction: only if parent is member of a particular group, race or religion) and A02b (birth in country to a parent born there: No provision), as its codebook (RSC/GLOBALCIT 2025/01, sections 3.2.1a to 3.2.2b) defines them: by birth in the territory only on the condition the dataset states; by descent from either parent, a child born abroad on the limit the dataset states. The coding also records a restriction to members of a particular group, which the form holds only in the condition's words, which the form doesn't hold. Changes to the law at birth after 1 January 2024 weren't checked for this file. On 2026-11-03 the primary was read: חוק האזרחות, תשי"ב-1952 (Nationality Law 5712-1952) as enacted, Sefer HaChukim, Knesset document server fs.knesset.gov.il (5 pages); its text layer runs in visual order, quoted here in logical order. It confirmed the years of residence, renunciation, loss on taking another citizenship and descent. It was silent on birth in the territory and the limit abroad, which still rest on the sources above, re-read that day and found the same. Only the 1952 text as enacted was read; its later amendments (to ss. 4 and 4A among others), where the conditional birth route and the limit abroad sit, weren't.

sources.title: GLOBALCIT Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (Vink, van der Baaren, Bauböck, Dzankic, Honohan, Manby; EUI Research Data, 2025), country-year-mode files, Israel, 2024
sources.said: Person is in Israel and has been resident there for 3 out of the 5 years immediately preceding the day of the submission of the application. Person is entitled to reside in Israel permanently, has settled (or intends to settle) in Israel. ... Person must have renounced citizenship of another country or proven his/her willingness to do so upon becoming a citizen. ... n.a. ... Generally applicable provision ... Person is born in Israel to a citizen. Children born after the death of their Israeli parent(s) will also be able to acquire Israel citizenship. ... Generational transmission restriction: conditional on birthplace/place of residence /mode under which parent acquired citizenship ... Person is born abroad to a citizen in one of the manners prescribed in paragraphs a-e. Transmission only to first generation abroad. Children born after the death of their Israeli parent(s) will also be able to acquire Israel citizenship. ... Group restriction: only if parent is member of a particular group, race or religion ... Person is born in Israel after the establishment of the State (citizenship 'by return'). This only applies if at least one parent was registered in the Population Register at the time of the person's birth (see ISR 2(c)(5)). The clause means that the 1950 Law of Return only applies to these individuals, who must necessarily be Jewish). It does not provide a form of ius soli. ... No provision

sources.title: חוק האזרחות, תשי"ב-1952 (Nationality Law 5712-1952) as enacted, Sefer HaChukim, Knesset document server fs.knesset.gov.il (5 pages); its text layer runs in visual order, quoted here in logical order
sources.said: 4. מי שנולד כשאביו או אמו היו אזרחים ישראליים, יהיה לאזרח ישראלי מלידה ... 5. (א) בגיר שאיננו אזרח ישראלי יכול לקבל אזרחות ישראלית על ידי התאזרחות אם נתקיימו בו תנאים אלה: (1) נמצא בישראל; (2) היה בישראל שלוש שנים מתוך תקופת חמש שנים שקדמה ליום הגשת בקשתו; (3) זכאי לשבת בישראל ישיבת קבע; (4) השתקע בישראל או שיש בדעתו להשתקע בה; (5) יודע מה-ידיעת את השפה העברית; (6) ויתר על אזרחותו הקודמת או הוכיח שיחדל מהיות אזרח חוץ לכשיהיה לאזרח ישראלי. ... 14. (א) פרט לענין התאזרחות, אין רכישת אזרחות ישראלית תלויה בויתור על אזרחות קודמת. (ב) אזרח ישראלי שהוא גם אזרח חוץ, רואים אותו, לענין חוקי ישראל, כאזרח ישראלי.

atBirth.soilIf: Person is born in Israel after the establishment of the State (citizenship 'by return'). This only applies if at least one parent was registered in the Population Register at the time of the person's birth (see ISR 2(c)(5)). The clause means that the 1950 Law of Return only applies to these individuals, who must necessarily be Jewish). It does not provide a form of ius soli.
atBirth.descentAbroad: Person is born abroad to a citizen in one of the manners prescribed in paragraphs a-e. Transmission only to first generation abroad. Children born after the death of their Israeli parent(s) will also be able to acquire Israel citizenship.
